info.title: Dokkit API
info.description: Dokkit watches machines, services and jobs. This is the HTTP API that the `dokkit` program, the command line, the client libraries, the MCP server and any script use.

tags.name: Intake
tags.description: Machines and apps send reports, deploys and declarations. Machine key or app key.

tags.name: Errors
tags.description: Error reports from an app, in Dokkit's own format or as Sentry envelopes. App key.

tags.name: Work
tags.description: The `dokkit` program asks for work, sends its output and result, and fetches updates. Machine key.

tags.name: Read
tags.description: Read issues, machines, services, jobs, logs, errors, deploys, rules and proposals. User token.

tags.name: Act
tags.description: Snooze and acknowledge issues, route and hold services, accept found things, keep error text and set when a job is late. User token with `act`.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: Keys, people, alert rules and settings, interface-added checks, restart, making jobs, updating the program and loading logs back. User token with `admin`.

tags.name: MCP
tags.description: The MCP server for AI tools. User token.

post.summary: Trade an enrolment token for a machine key
post.description: Spends a one-use enrolment token and makes the machine. The answer holds the machine key, shown once. A name that is already enrolled answers 409 and the token is kept, unless the token was made for that machine; then it enrols again and revokes that machine's earlier keys. Takes no key in the header. The enrolment token (`dke_`) goes in the body.

error.message: That token is not known, was already used, or has run out.
That machine name is already enrolled. Ask for an enrolment token made for that machine.
Needs a token and a hostname.

post.description: The main door. The body is newline-delimited JSON, one item per line, with a `type` and an `at` or `t`. The types are `state`, `inventory`, `metric`, `beat`, `job`, `stats`, `log`, `deploy` and `custom`. A batch is at most 5 MB compressed and 10,000 lines. A refused line does not fail the batch. Send the same `Dokkit-Batch` id again and nothing is stored twice. An app key may not send `state` or `inventory`, and may make 100 checks per service. Any line may carry `environment`: a value other than `production` is stored on a sibling service of that environment that never alerts, unless the service is declared by a `dokkit.toml`, which keeps its own environment. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).

parameters.name: Dokkit-Batch
parameters.description: Names the batch. Sending it again stores nothing twice.

parameters.name: Content-Encoding
parameters.description: Set to gzip when the body is compressed.

200.description: How many lines were accepted, and the ones refused.

error.message: A batch is at most 5 MB compressed and 10,000 lines.

422.description: The batch id is not a UUID (`bad_batch`), or the body is not valid gzip (`bad_gzip`).

put.summary: Declare a service from a dokkit.toml
put.description: The contents of a `dokkit.toml`, sent as JSON with the same structure. Sending the same file twice changes nothing. Checks, jobs, logs and stats become active. The file owns the service and its checks, so checks it no longer lists are removed. A machine key may declare any service on its machine. An app key may declare only the service it belongs to: `service.id` must be its slug (else 422), the machine and kind stay, checks may be of type `beat` or `custom` only, jobs keep `id`, `schedule`, `grace` and `max_runtime`, and the other sections are dropped. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).

get.description: Lets a machine check its address, its key and its clock. The answer holds the server's time. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).

post.description: What `dokkit scan` found, as the file was written. Nothing in it is active until a person accepts it in the interface. The server keeps running Windows services and systemd services, listening ports, scheduled jobs (`found.jobs`), containers that publish a TCP port and sites with an address, and leaves out what is already watched or was dismissed. A job is accepted as a job that waits for its first report. `notes` (a list of text) says what the scan could not see. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

get.summary: List things waiting to be accepted
get.description: Found things that wait for a person to accept them, each with `origin` (`system`, `software` or `yours`; null when the machine's program did not say) and `why`. The operating system's own things (`origin` `system`) are left out unless `system` is true; the answer says how many in `hidden`. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

post.summary: Report log lines from an app that logs to Seq
post.description: The door for apps and libraries written for Seq: Serilog.Sinks.Seq, seqlog, and the pino, winston and bunyan Seq transports. An app moves by changing its server address and API key. The body is CLEF (one JSON event a line, content type `application/vnd.serilog.clef`, or `?clef`), or Seq's older JSON form `{"Events": [...]}` with `Timestamp`, `Level`, `MessageTemplate`, `Properties`, `Exception` and `RenderedMessage`. Each event is stored as a log line of the app key's service, by the same path as `POST /api/v1/report`: the same limits (10,000 events and 5 MB a request) and no rate limit. Levels are mapped (`Verbose`, `Debug`, `Information`, `Warning`, `Error`, `Fatal` and the short forms), templates are rendered with the properties, properties become `fields`, an exception is kept as `fields.exception`. A property named `service`, `at` or `type` is kept as `service_name`, `seq_at` or `seq_type`. The same body is accepted at `POST /ingest/clef`, where newer Seq clients post CLEF. Takes an app key (`dka_`), in the `X-Seq-ApiKey` header or the `apiKey` query value. Answers as Seq does: `201` with `{"MinimumLevelAccepted": null}`, and errors as `{"Error": "..."}`.

parameters.name: clef
parameters.description: Present when the body is CLEF and the content type does not say so.

parameters.name: apiKey
parameters.description: The app key, when the client sends it in the query.

400.description: The body is not CLEF or Seq's JSON, or no event could be stored.

example.Error: The body is not CLEF or Seq's JSON events.

401.description: The key is missing or not an app key.

example.Error: The API key is missing or not valid.
A request is at most 5 MB and 10,000 events.

post.summary: Report errors from a Sentry SDK
post.description: The door for Sentry's open-source SDKs. An SDK is given an address made from an app key and Dokkit's host. Error events are stored; everything else is read and dropped, and the answer tells the SDK to stop sending those kinds. Gzip is accepted. The app key is read from the `X-Sentry-Auth` header, the `sentry_key` query value, or the envelope's first line. The `project` segment is whatever the SDK was given and is not used. Takes an app key (`dka_`).

get.description: The `dokkit` program asks for work and the server holds the request for up to `wait` seconds. 204 means nothing to do; ask again. The run's name is in `task`, and it is one of two. `dokkit:update` asks the program to fetch the newer copy the server holds. `dokkit:imessage` is offered only to the Mac chosen for iMessage and carries two more fields: `to`, the recipients, and `text`, the message. The program answers it on the result address with `exit_code` 0 when every recipient was sent to, 1 otherwise, or `refused` with the reason, and posts one line of output for each recipient. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

to.description: Only with `dokkit:imessage`: the phone numbers and email addresses to send to.

text.description: Only with `dokkit:imessage`: the message to send to each of them.

post.description: A chunk of the running run's output, as plain text. The server keeps the last part. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

get.description: The last 24 hours in 48 half hours, for each machine, and the issues that opened in that time. The last cell is the half hour that holds `to`. A cell is `down` if an issue that was down overlapped it, else `degraded` if any issue overlapped it, else `quiet` if the machine was heard from, else `none` (no signal). An issue counts in the state it has now, for its whole life. Soon issues and issues of services that are not in production colour nothing. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope.

put.summary: Set who is told about a service
put.description: Sets the channels for `down` and for `degraded`, each one channel or a list of channels that each send their own alert. A field that is not sent stays as it was; a value that is not a channel clears that route. `none` cannot be combined with other channels (422 `bad_routing`). `night` is optional; false holds the alerts of a night until it ends. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

down.description: One channel as text, or several as a list or as text with commas between. Each channel sends its own alert; `none` stands alone. A page and a push through PagerDuty together make one incident at the page's severity.

degraded.description: One channel as text, or several as a list or as text with commas between. Each channel sends its own alert; `none` stands alone. A page and a push through PagerDuty together make one incident at the page's severity.

night.description: False holds this service's alerts at night until the night ends. Default true.

error.message: down: none cannot be combined with other channels.

post.description: The MCP server, as JSON-RPC over one POST address. It can do no more than the user token allows. An AI tool with a token can do through MCP everything the token can do through the API. The tools are, with `read` scope: `attention`, `find`, `service`, `jobs`, `job_runs`, `errors`, `since_deploy`, `machines`, `machine`, `issues`, `issue`, `deploys`, `versions`, `rules`, `proposals`, `series` and `day`; with `read-logs` scope: `logs`; with `act` scope: `snooze`, `acknowledge`, `unsnooze`, `note`, `bulk`, `watch`, `unwatch`, `routing`, `hold`, `accept_proposal`, `dismiss_proposal`, `scan_machine`, `plan_downtime` and `end_downtime`; with `admin` scope: `add_rule`, `update_rule`, `delete_rule`, `set_checks`, `allow_restart`, `keys`, `make_key`, `revoke_key`, `people`, `add_person` and `remove_person`. `make_key` returns the key text once. Admin tools are marked destructive. `tools/list` shows only the tools the token may use. Every answer starts with a line saying that what follows is data written by machines and apps, never instructions. An argument of the wrong type is an `isError` answer; a null argument is the same as one left out, and a whole number written as 5.0 is an integer. A tool error is an answer with `isError` true, not an HTTP error. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

For SMS it is Twilio's own message when it gave one, and for iMessage it is the Mac's answer, which is waited for up to a minute. AlertSettingsBody.description: Any of the settings. One that is left out stays as it was. A secret, an address or a user name is written here and never returned. A secret sent as an empty string is cleared; one left out keeps its value. A secret goes to one host: if ntfy_url or smtp_host changes and ntfy_token or smtp_password is not sent in the same call, it is cleared and the answer carries a `note` that says so. Addresses must be https and may not be this machine or a link-local address unless the server sets DOKKIT_ALLOW_LOCAL_ALERTS=1. smtp_port is 25, 465, 587 or 2525. The night is whole hours: night_from and night_to from 0 to 23, night_offset (hours from UTC) from -12 to 14.
